# Introduction

*Pages PDF 4-19*

## Introduction
## **Orcs and Goblins**
Throughout the world, many scattered tribes of Orcs and Goblins exist. They are united by their shared ancenstry, cultures, a love of slaughter and mayhem, and a unifying spirit known to them as Waaagh! Aggression and cruelty are elemental to the character of Orcs and Goblins. Their only purpose is to wage war and celebrate the defeat and subjugation of their enemies. Denied a common foe, Orcs and Goblins soon grow bored and fractious and soon turn on one another with the same degree of viciousness with which they persecute Humans and Dwarfs. 

The term Orcs and Goblins describes a variety of related species, including Black Orcs, Gnoblars, Hobgoblins, Snotlings, and more. Because of the incredible variety of creatures that may be found in Orc and Goblin tribes, this book does not give an overview of Orc and Goblin society as a whole — such a society does not exist coherently. Instead, a broad overview of the creatures is given, together with a closer look at particular tribes and how they might work in games of **WFRP** . 

To other species, Orcs and Goblins are a scourge. Their armies despoiled Human nations several times, and they overran and infested much of the territory that was once part of the Everlasting Realm of the Dwarfs. Even the High Elven kingdoms of Ulthuan have suffered from the invasions of Goblins. 

On rare occasions, desperate marcher lords may try to use the aggressiveness of Orcs and Goblins. There are influential mercenary companies, such as Ruglud’s Armoured Orcs, Ghazak Khan’s Blackwolf Mercenaries, and Manglar’s Mutant Goblins. Still, it would be unwise to rely on such troops in the long term, and the citizens of towns they garrison often end up as rations. 

## **Tribes**
Orcs and Goblins live in tribes ranging from a few hundred individuals to thousands of warriors. A tribe usually contains Orcs and Goblins of the same type. It might be a Night Goblin tribe, a Black Orc tribe, a Forest Goblin tribe, and so on. However, many Orc tribes also include Goblins, who serve as lackeys, dogsbodies, and scouts. To further complicate matters, Orcs and Goblins often recruit monsters with appropriately ferocious temperaments, such as Squigs, Giants, and Trolls, and may pay for Ogre mercenaries to join their ranks. 

A chieftain called a Warboss or, with enough success, a Warlord leads a tribe. With victory, other Orcs and Goblins flock to join, and other tribes place themselves under his command. This phenomenon, whereby the success of a tribe influences others to enter it in a coalition, is known as Waaagh! The warband grows in strength, influence, and belligerence until it either sweeps its enemies before it in violent conquest or picks a fight with an enemy force it cannot beat, after which the bedraggled survivors split into smaller, bickering factions. 

Orc and Goblin tribes are dependent for their fortunes on the abilities of their chieftain. Tribes grow and become powerful under brave and successful leaders only to shrink or break apart when their chieftain is eventually defeated or slain. 

When a tribe breaks apart, the central portion continues under the old leader or his successor if the original boss died. The contenders for a tribe’s leadership come from the group of hulking elite Orcs known as Big‘Uns — a ruling class among the Orcs. Every tribe has a core of Big‘Uns waiting for their chance to take over. Of course, there can only be one chieftain, so defeated rivals must either accept his supremacy or leave the tribe altogether and set up a new one. 

## **History**
Orcs and Goblins do not keep historical records. The closest they have to scholarship are oral traditions passed down amongst their Shamans. However, these accounts are tribal histories rather than those of Orcs and Goblins as a whole and vary greatly. Most Orcs and Goblins do not care where they came from or how they relate to significant events that shaped the world. There is little teleology to Orc and Goblin culture. They rarely innovate new ideas or technology and quickly revert to simple, tried and tested lifestyles when placed under duress. 

Other species care little about the origins of Orcs and Goblins and the development of their culture. To more civilised races, Orcs and Goblins are simply a menace to be endured or eradicated. When written histories broach the subject of Orcs and Goblins, they speak of them in much the same way as natural disasters such as earthquakes or floods — destructive forces that occasionally cause widespread devastation (a view Orcs and Goblins might regard with pride were they to consider it). To scholars of the Empire, Orc and Goblin history is just a list of invasions suffered and campaigns fought. The Dwarfs keep records of the depredations of Orcs and Goblins, for the creatures have shattered many of the Dwarfs’ most prized Karaks. Still, while their records are more comprehensive than those of Humans, they do not trouble to concern themselves with the perspective of their enemies. 

The Elves and the Slann know a little more. They claim that Orcs and Goblins first appeared circa –10,000 IC. Their presence is supposed to be some unintended consequence of the Old Ones’ voyages from distant stars. 

Some tribes of Orcs and Goblins may well remember particularly successful Warlords and their conquests, though they do so only to measure themselves against such achievements. 

To an Orc, the fact that Gorbad Ironclaw razed much of the Empire might be an inspiration, but the fact that his Waaagh! took place between 1707 and 1712 IC would be dismissed as boring trivia. 

## **Culture and Belief**
Orcs and Goblins are not deep or original thinkers, and despite the number and variety of their tribes, they tend to resemble one another in their culture. They know little of agriculture, though Goblins and Snotlings may farm edible fungi and employ a cruel form of animal husbandry focused on raising beasts of war. They do know how to hunt and forage but get most of what they require through raiding and pillage. 

Orcs and Goblins know enough of carpentry, metalworking, leatherworking, and engineering to construct crude but effective fortifications, armour, and weaponry. They can fabricate machines such as chariots, stone throwers, and bolt throwers. However, their designs are simple and ramshackle, and an Orc stone thrower made in 2514 IC is no more sophisticated than one made thousands of years ago. 

Orcs and Goblins worship many gods, many of which are specific to particular tribes. However, tribes from all over the world, even those with no contact with other tribes, worship a pair of gods, giant Orc brothers. These are Gork, who embodies brutality with an edge of cunning, and Mork, who embodies cunning with an edge of brutality. 

## **Orcs, Goblins, and Chaos**
Orcs and Goblins do not tend to suffer greatly from the corruption of Chaos. They are not entirely immune to its influence but do not trouble themselves about it as Humans and Elves do. An Orc might respect followers of Khorne for their devotion to war and bloodshed, but their gods provide all the inspiration for bloodshed and mayhem that they need. 

Mutation is not unknown amongst Orcs and Goblins. For the main part they do not persecute mutants. If a mutation weakens an Orc it may be reviled, but if a mutation grants an Orc an edge in combat it is respected. 

On occasion, Daemons may be worshipped by Orcs and Goblins who encounter them, but this is due to their size and power rather than the principles they embody. 

## **Orc and Goblin Animosity**
Orcs and Goblins are so bellicose that they attack one another to stave off boredom or establish a pecking order. Tribal chiefs are used to such behaviour and dismiss it as petty squabbling. Most Orcs and Goblins have the _Animosity (Greenskins)_ Creature Trait. This is not to suggest that Orcs and Goblins are less hostile to other species — quite the opposite — but that even erstwhile cohorts bicker. Orcs and Goblins usually constrain their animosity to crude insults or brief bouts of fisticuffs, but the violence can become injurious. 

Opponents of Orcs and Goblins can use this tendency against them, by denying them a straight fight, setting them against each other, or presenting evidence (real or fabricated) that some members plan to undermine or attack others. If Characters contrive a situation in which a group of Orcs and Goblins might squabble, have the leader of the group make a **Challenging (+0) Leadership** Test. If the test is failed, roll on the table below. 

This tactic does not work in situations where there is a clear and present danger to the Orcs and Goblins, if _Hatred_ a Character who the Orcs and Goblins suffer against, or who subjects them to _Fear_ or _Terror,_ is in the vicinity, or if the Orcs and Goblins are being led by a Black Orc. 

The leader of a group may make further Leadership Tests each Round to stop the violence. These tests suffer from a –2 SL penalty if the group includes a Hobgoblin.

## **Territory**
Orc and Goblin tribes are found across the world. However, but for the exception of the Hobgoblin Khanate far to the east of the Old World, they have no stable bases of power. A particular tribe may inhabit the same region for generations, and a particular Warlord may command thousands of warriors, but there is no central authority to deal with or appeal to, and arrangements with Orc and Goblin chiefs change on a whim. 

As far as folk of the Old World are concerned, Orcs and Goblins are most commonly found in the Dark Lands to the east of the Worlds Edge Mountains, and the Badlands south of the Border Princes. It is no coincidence that these regions were populated by Dwarfs, who established holds and fortresses in their mountain ranges. Following their war with the Elves, the Dwarfs were much depleted and suffered further calamity due to a series of earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and the depredations of the Skaven. 

Orcs and Goblins propagate easily in these lands and had already often warred with Dwarfs by this time. The Dwarfs speak of the years between –1500 IC and the coming of Sigmar as the Goblin Wars. During this time, many of their most celebrated holds were besieged and overrun. The Orcs and Goblins who now infest the shattered watchtowers, forts, and underground cities of the Dwarfs benefit from redoubtable strongholds where it is impossible to effectively assail them. 

The Human nations have had more luck in ridding their lands of Orcs and Goblins. Both Sigmar in the Empire and Gilles de Breton in Bretonnia more or less marked the founding of their nations by driving out the Orcs and Goblins that lived there, though small tribes still persist among forest deeps and mountain peaks. In the Empire, many Forest Goblin tribes can be found in the woodlands, and even haunt the Reikwald around Altdorf. In Bretonnia, the Massif Orcal is so named for the many Orc and Goblin tribes who resist the best efforts of questing knights to wipe them out. 

In Tilea and Estalia, Orcs and Goblins are more of a presence, though mostly kept under control. Even so, their numbers in the Appucini Mountains and the Vaults can prove a problem. In the Border Princes, Human states are more parlous, and the lands claimed by a petty marcher lord and the territory of an established Orc or Goblin tribe often lie uncomfortably close to one another. 

## **Goblins**
Goblins are small, scrawny, cruel-hearted, and possessed of low cunning. They flourish in nearly every environment in the world, though they inhabit the Badlands and Dark Lands in particular profusion. Goblins exist in several sub-types, which are culturally distinct from one another. All Goblins possess waxy green skins, small sharp teeth, long pointed ears, and beady red eyes. 

## **Common Goblins**
The most widespread type of Goblin are known as Common Goblins. They work leather and metal, and their warbands typically consist of troops armed with spears supported by contingents of archers. Many Common Goblins capture and ride giant wolves into battle and sometimes use them to pull light chariots. 

While Goblins are cunning in their way — they do show some ability to learn the languages and tactics of other species — they are not particularly innovative, and their ability to engineer machinery seems limited to constructing rickety machines for the purposes of siegecraft, warfare, and torture. 

Goblins are garrulous and propagate quickly, though their innately spiteful dispositions usually prevent them from cooperating with one another unless they have a common enemy to focus their ire upon. 

Goblin bands raid for food, booty, and the sheer love of slaughter. They tend to shun away from straight fights, preferring to confront their opponents only when they outnumber them. Goblins delight in cruelty and will soon prey upon one another if they have no common enemy to fight. 

Goblins find Elves unnerving and repugnant, possibly due to the Elves’ habits of cleanliness and civilised manners. Goblins very much dislike fighting Elves and tend to avoid them if possible. 

Armour involves various bits of scavenged leather and armour, and wooden or leather shields. Goblins do not possess the skill or patience to make mail but will cobble looted armour together. Weapons are usually crude swords, though spears are also commonly employed. Many Goblins prefer to fight with bows and have the _Ranged +6 (50)_ Trait. 

## **Gnoblars**
Gnoblars, also known as Hill Goblins, are a breed of Goblin common to the lands east of the Dark Lands. They are smaller and thinner than Common Goblins and even less inclined to craftsmanship, preferring to scavenge and barter for equipment and weaponry rather than make anything themselves. 

In the distant past, Hill Goblins were thoroughly subjugated by other Orcs and Goblins and the Chaos Dwarfs. However, many of their tribes have entered a mutually beneficial relationship with the Ogres of the Mountains of Mourn, providing service as dogsbodies in exchange for protection. This relationship has proved lasting, probably because the Ogres find the meat of Gnoblars foul, stringy, and meagre in terms of portion. 

Gnoblars tend not to wear any armour or use shields. They are not militarily minded, and their Ogre masters would not consider it a good use of time to train them. They fight with crude clubs and stolen knives and have a predilection for using slings, providing them with the _Ranged +6 (60)_ Trait. 

Gnoblars do not tend to manifest much in the way of individual talent, and have no ability to employ Waaagh! magic. A Gnoblar may not make use of the Warlord, Shaman, or Shaman Lord templates. 

## **Forest Goblins**
Forest Goblins can be found in the woodlands of the Old World and the jungles of equatorial regions. They tend to lack the skills or opportunities to work metal and leather, and instead create equipment and weaponry crafted from bone, wood, claws, and teeth. 

Many Forest Goblin tribes use Giant Spiders as mounts and war beasts, and their Shamans are particularly potent due to the magical qualities of certain spider venoms. 

Armour tends to be limited to a rawhide shield, though some Forest Goblins accessorise with spider carapace, bones, and mail stolen from their victims. Weapons are usually axes or swords, though spears are also commonly employed. Many Goblins prefer to fight from a distance and have the _Ranged +6 (50)_ Trait in addition to those listed below. 

Night Goblins tend not to manufacture or wear armour, though they do craft suits of mail or scale for their leaders. Most of them carry small round shields for protection. They arm themselves with swords or spears. Night Goblins make capable archers and may have the _Ranged +6 (50)_ Trait in addition to those listed below. 

Night Goblin soldiers and elites may also be equipped with nets and two-handed weapons such as squig prodders (treat these as Halberds) or massive wooden clubs (treat as Two-Handed Warhammers). 

## **Other Types**
There are rumours of other types of Goblin adapted to living in meres, deserts, or volcanic regions. These forms of Goblin are little understood by Human scholars, and confirmation that they are seperate types with peculiar physiology, or simply Common Goblins or Gnoblars that have adapted to their environments, is unknown. 

## **Night Goblins**
Night Goblins inhabit tunnels and caves in the vast mountain ranges of the world. They are used to the dark and find the sun’s light uncomfortable and unnerving. They wear dark hooded robes to protect themselves from the sunlight, which lends them their distinctive appearance. 

Night Goblins tend to be smaller and more lithe than Common Goblins and are even more cowardly in the face of danger. They live alongside other creatures that make their homes in the world’s dark places, such as Stone Trolls and varieties of Squig. Night Goblins have learned methods of war suited to their subterranean environment, such as using nets to entangle their opponents or herding wild squigs toward their enemies. 

The Shamans of Night Goblin tribes use a variety of toxic mushrooms that flourish in their caves. Some of these fungi have magical properties and assist in spellcasting. Others, such as the notorious Mad Cap Mushrooms, are given to the Night Goblin warriors known as Fanatics to make them ferocious and powerful in combat and to dull their senses of fear and pain. 

Armies of Night Goblins have fought many wars against the Dwarfs and have come to regard them with particularly bitter hatred. They also come into occasional contact with Skaven, sometimes cooperating with the secretive ratmen and sometimes making war on them.

## **Orcs**
Orcs are related to Goblins but are less common, particularly in the Old World, where Humans have campaigned to eradicate them. Unlike Goblins, which can be found in the depths of the forests of the Empire, Orcs cling on only in the mountainous regions and there in small, scattered communities. There are more Orcs in the Dark Lands and the Badlands, though they are not found in the same number as Goblins. This is a blessing, for Orcs are a more dangerous prospect, being larger, tougher, stronger, and more inclined to organise effective military forces. 

Orcs are less inclined to be petty and spiteful than Goblins, but they are warlike, filled with a desire to conquer and dominate. In each other’s company, their aggression and belligerence may take on the appearance of boisterous humour and vigorous competition. Still, whilst the Orc love of violence might be couched in the appearance of rough sport, they have a bloodthirsty nature. 

An Orc may regard his fellows with fraternal affection if they have a clear common purpose (usually, this purpose is to make war against the nearest convenient enemy). If they become bored or directionless, they begin to argue amongst themselves, and bloody fights are the inevitable consequence of these disputes. 

While Orcs craft little of their own armour, they take war seriously enough to cobble together suits of mail and leather with large, iron-rimmed shields. They fight with crude hand weapons that are heavier than the equivalent weapons carried by other species, called ‘choppas’ by the Orcs. Some sneakier Orcs prefer to fight with bows and have the _Ranged +6 (50)_ Trait. 

## **Savage Orcs**
Some Orc tribes demonstrate a pronounced frustration with (or superstition against) technological innovation. This may be due to unpleasant ancestral experiences with Dwarfs or Chaos Dwarfs, isolation from other Orc tribes, or a quirk of how the Orc metabolism reacts to prolonged heat and humidity (both Lustria and the Southlands are plagued by Savage Orc tribes). 

These Orcs eschew even the crude metalworking and engineering skills developed by typical Orcs and are known as Savage Orcs. They arm themselves with simple weapons made of stone or bone and daub themselves with protective warpaint. They are known for being fearless and fierce fighters. 

Savage Orcs believe their warpaint attracts the favour of _Ward_ the Orc gods, Gork and Mork. They possess the _10_ Trait to represent this faith. Should a Savage Orc be deprived of warpaint, or lose his faith it, then he will also lose the Ward 10 Trait. 

Savage Orcs wear no armour other than a simple shield. They use weapons carved from bone or flint. They use bows and may have the _Ranged +6 (50)_ Trait.

The Chaos Dwarfs keep hundreds of Orcs and Goblins in servitude in the Dark Lands, forcing them to labour in their mines and factories. Their sorcerers are suspected of breeding the first Black Orcs, intending for them to be a more robust and disciplined strain than the typical Orcs. If the Chaos Dwarfs did produce the first Black Orcs they probably came to regret their decision, as Black Orcs are headstrong and independently-minded. A massive rebellion of Chaos Dwarf slaves is thought to have occurred in the decades before Sigmar’s birth and may have been led by the recalcitrant Black Orcs. 

Black Orcs are not commonly encountered, though there are rumours that entire tribes of the creatures can be found deep in the Dark Lands. In the Badlands bands of Black Orcs can be found wandering from tribe to tribe. In the main, they join a tribe for a while before becoming irritated with the lack of discipline and dedication to war that they perceive in other Orcs and Goblins and move on, looking for a tribe with more potential. Should they find a tribe whose commitment to war suits their own, they will seek to dominate it, ousting the old leaders and setting their own chieftain up in his stead. 

## **Black Orcs**
Black Orcs hail from the heart of the Dark Lands and are feared as the largest and most antagonistic of all breeds of Orc. They are larger and more heavily built than typical Orcs. They are usually bedecked in heavy plate armour and carry brutal choppas or two-handed weapons. 

Black Orcs are so called because their skins are darker than those of typical Orcs, either a deep shade of green or black. It could also refer to the demeanour, as they are grim and humourless. 

Black Orcs were first reported in the Empire shortly before the birth of Sigmar. A band of them crossed the Worlds Edge Mountains and conquered a tribe of Orcs living in the hilly country to the north of what is now known as Stirland. When Sigmar united the tribes of men and waged war to expel the Orcs from the Empire, those battles he fought against the tribes led by Black Orcs were the most desperate. 

Black Orcs typically fight as blocks of heavy infantry. They may take the Soldier or Elite template but may not be Skirmishers. Black Orc Shamans are unheard of, as they embody Gork and Mork in their martial discipline and do not manifest magical abilities. They may take the Chief or Warlord template. 

Black Orcs always help themselves to the best military equipment from piles of war booty, and unlike other Orcs and Goblins, they will trouble themselves to craft and maintain suits of mail. They tend to arm themselves with heavy broad-bladed choppas but may exchange these weapons with a two-handed axe or maul. They do not use missile weapons. 

Other Orcs and Goblins are intimidated by Black Orcs, aware that their larger cousins have little patience for nonsense. They tend not to indulge in squabbles or mischief making when Black Orcs are in the vicinty. 

## **Basic Black Orc**
The origins of Black Orcs are mysterious, but their association with the Dark Lands and their appearance in the Empire around the time of Sigmar lead some scholars to suppose the Chaos Dwarfs may be responsible.

## **Hobgoblins**
Hobgoblins are rare and unwelcome visitors to the Old World. They have a reputation for being the vilest and most treacherous of all the Goblin and Orc kin. They are taller than Goblins and scrawnier than Orcs, with narrow eyes and sneering mouths. Unlike Goblins and Orcs, Hobgoblins grow thick hair, which they typically wear long, lank, and greasy, or tied up into topknots. 

The Hobgoblin homelands are the steppelands to the east of the Worlds Edge Mountains and north of the Dark Lands, an area of scattered forest and vast, flat grassland. Here the Hobgoblins live in wandering tribes, all of which are vassals to the ruling Mourngul tribe. The chief of the Mournguls is the great Hobgobla Khan, despotic leader of the Hobgoblin hordes and undisputed ruler of the steppes. He is heir to the victories of the legendary Khengai Khan, the Mourngul chief who first confederated the tribes of the steppes. His massed regiments of wolfriding cavalry defy the marauder tribes who also travel the steppes, and raid outlying settlements of Grand Cathay. 

These steppe Hobgoblins are cruel and treacherous, though they practice a form of honour culture that is alien to most Orcs and Goblins, with a taste for solving disputes through single combat. 

Hobgoblins often work as mercenaries, making particularly effective scouts and skirmishers from the back of their giant wolf mounts. They are by no means reliable troops, but unlike Orcs and Goblins, they do understand strategy and can refrain from treachery provided their employer makes it clear where their self-interest lies. Should the tide of a battle look likely to turn against their employer’s favour, or if an enemy makes them an attractive offer, Hobgoblin mercenaries are notorious for switching sides. 

The Chaos Dwarfs long ago adopted the Hobgoblins of the Dark Lands as their favoured lackeys. Unlike the Hobgoblins of the steppes, those who work for the Chaos Dwarfs are distinguished by being servile, craven, and even more thoroughly despicable. In the realm of the Chaos Dwarfs the Hobgoblins serve as overseers and toadies, ensuring that the captive Orcs and Goblins held in thrall by the Chaos Dwarfs are kept in line. 

Tales are told of a massive Orc and Goblin rebellion that took place in the forges and workshops of the Chaos Dwarfs’ dominion, a revolt that looked set to sweep their masters aside and end their wretched bondage. The treachery of the Hobgoblins saw to it that their Chaos Dwarf masters were informed of the growing revolt, and in the brutal reprisals that followed, the Hobgoblins took sadistic glee in punishing the recalcitrant elements and solidifying their position as lackeys to the Chaos Dwarfs. 

Orcs and Goblins loathe Hobgoblins even more than they loathe each other. Some of this hostility may be explained by the activities of those Hobgoblins who persecute Orcs and Goblins by the order of their Chaos Dwarf masters, but the ill feeling seems to run deeper, an innate tendency to despise Hobgoblins that goes beyond the normal animosity such creatures hold for one another. 

## **Basic Hobgoblin**
From time to time, Hobgoblin bands split off from the horde and range beyond the realm of the Khan, spreading terror and destruction. These rampaging bands are usually led by some lesser khan who has fallen out with the Hobgobla-Khan and fled beyond his domains.

## **Snotlings**
Snotlings are the smallest of the varied species related to Orcs and Goblins. They have little in the way of intelligence or personality, and whilst they manifest the spite and belligerence of larger Goblin-kin, they are more animalistic. Wherever Orcs and Goblins congregate in number, Snotlings may also be found. They tend to inhabit the midden heaps, waste pits, and darker corners of Orc caves and huts, scavenging from amongst their rubbish piles, and stealing anything they can get their hands on. They have an affinity with all things unhygienic, being highly resistant to poisons. 

Orcs, not normally known for their tolerance, tend to regard Snotlings as wayward pets, and in turn, the Snotlings fawn over their Orc masters. Provided instructions are clear, and explained in single syllables, Snotlings can be trained to perform tasks such as fetching and carrying or keeping watch. Snotlings can be craven bootlickers or capricious mimickers, depending on their mood, but providing that they are not stupid enough to mock Orcs, then Orcs can find them entertaining company. 

Goblins are less inclined to put up with Snotlings, seeing in their diminutive cousins the same bad habits they delight in themselves, such as petty vindictiveness, craven toadying, spiteful contempt, scatological obsession, and rampant kleptomania. 

Goblins find it difficult to sneak about, conspire to treachery, or indulge in wanton pilfering if there are Snotlings around, as they make shrill reports of suspicious activity to any superior who might take an interest. 

Snotlings are poor warriors, feeble, feral, and individually cowardly. When other Orcs and Goblins become warlike, the braver Snotlings become enthused, and band together in mobs, arming themselves with any sharp or heavy objects they can lay their hands on, such as broken branches, splintered bones, or pilfered knives. They make instinctive use of poisonous fungi, throwing ripe puffballs that explode to release poisonous clouds of spores. Whilst these rabbles are of dubious military application, their harassment can bog down an unwary enemy. 

Snotlings tend not to thrive in the wild, being dependent on Orcs and Goblins for protection and sustenance. On rare occasions, a band of Snotlings may infest the sets of badgers or foxes, turning them into noisome rotting dens, though these wild Snotlings are even more animalistic than those found in Orc camps. 

## **Snotlings, Equipment, and Templates**
Snotlings rarely manifest much in the way of potential. They do not craft their own weapons or armour, and no Orc or Goblin would waste time making military equipment for them or teaching them basic drill or discipline. A peculiarly talented Snotling may take the Skirmisher or Soldier template, but the only equipment they would benefit from would be throwing weapons such as knives, rocks, or javelins. 

## **Snotling Puffballs**
Snotlings enjoy a symbiotic relationship with a wide variety of fungi, and are largely immune to poisons as a result. Fungus forms much of their diet, but they also emply fungi as weaponry. 

In particular they make use of a type of puffball that may be thrown, counting as Rocks for the purpose of calculating Range and Damage. If an opponent takes _Venom_ a Wound from a puffball, they suffer from the _(Challenging)_ Creature Trait. 

**BASIC SNOTLING**

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|4|25|15|25|20|20|30|15|15|30|15|7|

**Traits:** Bestial, Dark Vision, Immunity (Poison), Infected, Size (Small), Weapon +4 

**Optional:** Swarm, Trained (Broken, Fetch, Guard), Venom (Challenging) 

Ogres are large creatures, a height of twelve feet is typical and they are broadly built. Ogres may look flabby and paunchy, but much of their bulk is hard muscle and they are enormously tough and powerful. Ogres have voracious appetites and suffer from pangs of hunger that they can sate only after copious feasting, and even then only for a short time. They have flat, overlapping teeth, and their muscular guts, of which they are immensely proud, digest flesh, bone, even scraps of metal, efficiently and quickly. Ogres crave meat and are often willing to be paid in flesh in lieu of gold. 

The love of feasting has a religious aspect, in that Ogres worship an atavistic god they call the Great Maw. Ogres go so far as to claim that the Great Maw is manifest upon the world. They say that there is a vast hole in the earth east of the Mountains of Mourn, and that this gaping cavern is lined with a pulsing gullet, ringed with many rows of sharp white teeth. Ogres believe this site to be the Great Maw itself, and they often make pilgrimages to the edge of the cavern, throwing hunks of meat into it in the hope of receiving its beneficence. 

## **Ogres**
Ogres are not related to Orcs and Goblins. They are, in fact, distant relatives of Humans and Halflings. However, their societies are similar to Orcs and Goblins in that they live in semi-nomadic tribes, are warlike and belligerent, and respect strength and ferocity as qualities in their leaders more readily than they do intelligence or vision. Because the roles played in Ogre society are roughly equivalent to those played in Orc and Goblin society, they are included in this book and use the same templates as Orcs and Goblins. 

Ogres live to the far east of the Empire in the Mountains of Mourn. They are regularly seen in foreign lands, including Human nations, as they often work as mercenaries. Ogres are said to suffer from a strange wanderlust, and rarely settle for long. However, mercenary commanders can find them disciplined and  effective troops. Ogres are not fussy about who they work for, and do not trouble themselves to consider whether or not they approve of the cause for which they fight. As long as they are provided with pay and opportunities for violence, they are happy. 

A caste of Ogres known as Butchers play a similar role as Shamans or Priests. They practice a debased form of magic incorporating the consumption of particular food and invoking the Great Maw. This magical lore is covered on page 82, though additional information can be found in **Archives of the Empire Volume 2** . Another caste of Ogre spellcasters are known as Firebellies, who derive their powers through the worship of a volcano known as the Fire Mouth, which the Ogres believe imbues a supplicant with magical power provided they survive an ordeal involving the consumption of molten lava. Firebellies can be made using the Shaman template and have access to spells from the Lore of Fire. Note that Ogres use Toughness rather than Intelligence for the basis of casting spells. 

Ogre leaders are known as Bruisers and their overlords as Tyrants, and can be represented by the Chief and Warlord templates respectively.

| 6 | 30 | 20 | 45 | 45 | 20 | 25 | 20 | 20 | 30 | 20 | 30 |

## **Trolls**
Trolls are hulking creatures with gangling limbs and stooped, misshapen bodies. They may look skinny, or even comically disproportioned, but they are tremendously strong, with heavy bones, bunched muscles, and sinews like cables. Trolls are hideous, slow-witted, and eternally hungry (even more so than Ogres). 

Trolls possess insatiable appetites and will eat food that even an Ogre would baulk at, including wood, rock, and bits of metal. The digestive juices of a Troll are considered one of the most corrosive substances in the world and are prized by alchemists and potion makers, although the risk of obtaining it seldom proves worthwhile. Trolls have even been known to use their vomit as a weapon, regurgitating over their foes when under duress. 

The gnarled hide of Trolls regrows almost as quickly as it is damaged. If a Troll’s hand is severed, a fresh one grows from the stump. If a Troll is decapitated, a new head forms on its shoulders. A great deal of damage must be inflicted upon a Troll to stop it regenerating. The only thing Trolls cannot endure is fire, and so burning a Troll is one sure way of killing it. 

Trolls are not related to Orcs and Goblins, but they are associated with them. Like Orcs and Goblins, they are found all over the world, though are most commonly encountered in mountains, caves, and untracked wilderness. Bands of Trolls often latch onto Orc or Goblin tribes, attracted by the profusion of carcasses and refuse. Orc bosses encourage them to stick around by tossing them the odd Snotling. Trolls can be fierce opponents in battle, but they are so dumb that they cannot be relied upon to understand even simple orders. When confronted with a determined opposition, they often stand around confused, or wander off in search of easier prey. 

Trolls do not use templates in the same way as Orcs and Goblins. See page 88 for a set of templates used to develop individual Trolls.

## **How to Use Templates**
In many cases, the basic creatures provided earlier in the book will work for combat encounters, however, as mentioned in **WFRP** , page 310, creatures are described as generic, and basic in their power level. To create a more impressive or powerful individual, a GM could use the career system from **WFRP** , but a simpler way to create a more powerful Orc, or a Goblin Shaman, would be to use templates here. 

To use a template, abide by the following process: 

- Choose a basic creature. 

## **Soldier**
The basic creature can represent soldiers in many cases, but many are more experienced fighters. 

**SOLDIER**

| M | WS | BS | S | T | I | Ag | Dex | Int | WP | Fel | W |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
||+5||+5|+5|+10||||+5|||

**Skills:** Cool +10, Dodge +10, Melee (Basic or Polearm) +10 

**Talents:** Combat Reflexes, Resolute

**Trappings:** Hand Weapon, Leather Armour, Shield, Spear

- Choose a template to apply to the creature, adding new Skills, Talents, Traits, and Trappings as appropriate. 

- Recalculate Wounds, as Strength, Toughness, and Willpower may well have improved. 

- Select a mount from page 19 if required. Add Ride (Any) +15 to the Skills of Characters with a mount.

## Shamans and _Armour_
For the most part, Shamans have the same problems with armour that Wizards do. When using the templates to create a Shaman, remove the _Armour_ Trait from the basic creature. 

## **Orc and Goblin Names**
There are no hard conventions when it comes to the names Orcs and Goblins go by. Young Orcs and Goblins tend not to be known by individual names, merely being referred to as ‘runt’ or ‘yoof ’ until they have proved themselves able to survive and contribute to the tribe. Upon achieving recognition, the Goblin or Orc will be given a name, or allowed to adopt one of their choosing. There is no sharp delineation between Orc names and Goblin names. The ones listed here are merely the names particular Orcs and Goblins have been reported as going by. Goblin names may tend to suit sneering higher pitched voices, and Orc names tend to suit deeper bellowing voices, but either species may adopt names from either list. Orcs and Goblins who have names incorporating the letter Z tend to be associated with Shamanism. 

Savage Orcs tend to use names of a single syllable. Snotlings also tend to use monosyllabic names, though the words they choose tend to be even more simple and bathetic than other Orc and Goblin names. 

Orcs and Goblins of note often choose a title for themselves, or have one chosen for them. Some of these titles may indicate primitive humour, and Goblins, in particular, seem to like titles that are alliterative, onomatopoeic, or bathetic. Titles often speak to a warrior’s prowess, a favoured weapon, or an act causing affront to the enemies of Orcs and Goblins.

## **Mounts**
The mounts used by Orcs and Goblins and similar creatures are as varied as Orcs and Goblins themselves, and usually suited to the environment within which the tribe spends most of its time. Plains-dwelling Common Goblins and Hobgoblins prefer fleet-footed wolves, whilst the Forest Goblins tend to capture and raise various breeds of Giant Spider as mounts, and Night Goblins may be able to train and capture bouncing Squigs.
